lines.trans: I have been living in Moscow for two weeks already.
Have you already gotten used to life in Moscow?
I came here from Voronezh for a dream.
And now you work in the best restaurant.
Claude Monet restaurant is the most famous in the city.
Here there are very strict rules and an expensive menu.
But for me this is wonderful experience.
And where did you find yourself housing?

words.gloss: yourself (в себе = in one's right mind)

lines.trans: I live right in the center of the city.
Apartments in the center cost huge money.
And I do not pay a single kopeck!
That sounds very strange and suspicious.
I have one secret plan.

words.gloss: there is (у меня есть = I have)

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'вестный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('famous, well-known').

examples.text: Он самый известный человек в городе.
examples.trans: He is the most famous man in town.

examples.text: Вы сами подумайте. Он самый известный человек в Синеозерске!
examples.trans: Think about it yourselves. He is the most famous man in Sineozersk!

examples.text: Он самый известный человек в Синеозерске!
examples.trans: He is the most famous man in Sineozersk!

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Also a flat number in an address. Common feminine noun meaning 'flat, apartment' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: on a phone or in a restaurant; indeclinable

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?

meanings.note: Сон is a dream while sleeping. Common feminine noun meaning 'dream, wish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, тебе сколько лет? Это глупые детские мечты.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, how old are you? Those are silly childish dreams.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

meanings.note: + genitive: ни копейки = not a penny
Core Russian part meaning 'not a (single); neither... nor' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

meanings.en: to get used to, become accustomed
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'выкнуть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get used to'.

examples.text: Я ещё не привык к Москве.
examples.trans: I am not used to Moscow yet.

examples.text: Ты уже привык к жизни в Москве?
examples.trans: Have you already gotten used to life in Moscow?
I got used to working by the law.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екретный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('secret').

examples.text: А почему он на секретном совещании?
examples.trans: And why is he at a secret meeting?

meanings.note: Сколько стоит? = how much is it?. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.

examples.trans: And how much does the console cost?

meanings.note: Как странно = how strange. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.
